title: Solve Systems by Elimination Review Test
description: Solve systems by adding or subtracting equivalent equations to eliminate one variable.

questions.questionText: Solve by elimination: 4x + 3y = 7 and -4x + 2y = 18. What is the solution?
questions.explanation: The x-terms are opposites, so adding the equations eliminates x. Solve for y, then substitute to find x.

questions.questionText: For 5x + 5y = 35 and -3x + 5y = 19, what happens if you subtract the second equation from the first?
questions.explanation: The y-coefficients match. Subtracting equations with matching y-terms makes the y-term become zero.

questions.questionText: Use elimination on 5x + 5y = 0 and -3x + 5y = 8. What x-value do you get after eliminating y?
questions.explanation: Subtract the equations to eliminate y, then divide by the remaining x-coefficient.

questions.questionText: Before eliminating x in 5x + 2y = 23 and 15x + 5y = 65, multiply the first equation by -3. Which equivalent equation results?
questions.explanation: Multiplying an equation by a factor means multiplying every term on both sides by that factor.

questions.questionText: After scaling one equation, solve by elimination: 3x - 3y = -12 and 6x + y = -31. What is the solution?
questions.explanation: Scale one equation so a pair of variable terms are opposites, add to eliminate that variable, then substitute back.

questions.questionText: Which first move is most efficient for 4x + 3y = -18 and -4x + 2y = 28?
options: divide both equations by the y-coefficients
questions.explanation: The x-coefficients are already opposites, so adding the equations is the efficient elimination step.

questions.questionText: Add 4x + 3y = -12 and -4x + 2y = -8 to eliminate x. What y-value is in the solution?
questions.explanation: Adding removes the x-terms. Solve the remaining one-variable equation for y.

questions.questionText: A system is 2x + 3y = -1 and -2x + 5y = -23. Why is multiplying an entire equation allowed before elimination?
options: it removes the need to check the second equation
it makes any chosen ordered pair correct
it changes the solution so the numbers are easier
multiply every term in one equation by the same factor
questions.correctAnswer: multiply every term in one equation by the same factor
questions.explanation: Multiplying both sides of an equation by the same nonzero factor creates an equivalent equation with the same solutions.

questions.questionText: A student used elimination and found x = -3. Which ordered pair solves 5x - y = -13 and 2x + 3y = -12?
questions.explanation: After finding one variable, substitute it into either original equation to find the other variable.

questions.questionText: After solving 2x - 5y = 23 and 6x + y = 21 by elimination, what is the best final check?
options: check only the equation that was multiplied
check the ordered pair in both original equations
make sure the two constants have the same sign
verify that the eliminated variable equals 0
questions.correctAnswer: check the ordered pair in both original equations
questions.explanation: A system solution must make every original equation true, so the final ordered pair should be checked in both equations.
